anomaly_def.Name: Schema and Index Design Anomaly + Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Schema and Index Design Anomaly : Table structures, indexes, partitioning, or data types are mismatched to workload access patterns, forcing inefficient access paths even when SQL is well written.
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Catalog statistics are stale, incomplete, or misleading, causing the optimizer to misestimate cardinalities and pick sub-optimal plans.
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : The database engine allocates more memory to caches and work areas than the host can safely supply, triggering OS pressure, paging, and cache churn.

When all three root causes coexist, the system shows a blend of symptoms: queries that should be index-seek driven are compiled into full scans because the needed indexes are missing or non-covering, while inaccurate statistics further mislead the optimizer into believing those scans are cheap. The resulting plans read far more pages than necessary, bloating buffer pools and spilling large hash and sort operations. Memory consumption rises rapidly, eroding cache hit ratios and provoking paging, temporary spill files, or out-of-memory terminations. Execution times become highly volatile: some requests stall on I/O, others throttle on memory grants, and background processes compete with the OS for RAM, causing node-level instability. Because each anomaly obscures the others, traditional tuning signals—such as adding an index or refreshing statistics—yield only partial relief and regress again under load.

Causal chain: Poor schema and index design creates inherently heavy I/O plans; stale or incomplete statistics hide their true cost and steer the optimizer toward even heavier plans; these bloated plans inflate memory grants and enlarge the working-set size of buffer and work areas. The swollen memory footprint pushes the host into sustained pressure, which in turn degrades cache efficiency and amplifies the I/O impact of the original design flaw. Meanwhile, memory pressure may delay or cancel automatic statistics collection, keeping statistics stale and completing a feedback loop that reinforces all three anomalies. The combined effect is a self-perpetuating degradation cycle that progressively worsens both latency and stability across OLTP and analytical workloads.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the amount of time after which a TCP keepalive message that has not been acknowledged by the client should be retransmitted.
entry.trigger_condition: A TCP keepalive probe is not acknowledged for tcp_keepalives_interval on systems supporting TCP_KEEPINTVL or an equivalent socket option.
entry.workload_impact: Controls retry timing for keepalive probes used to detect unresponsive client connections.
entry.default_behavior: Default value is 0, selecting the operating system default.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
